comments.text:
maybe the problem is the pet lover move didn't count as an accumulation space in BGA, therefore it conflict with Ravenous Hunger

Pet lover:
Each time you use an accumulation space providing exactly 1 animal, you can leave it on the space and get one from the general supply instead, as well as 3 <FOOD> and 1 <GRAIN>.
Ravenous Hunger:
Immediately after each time you use the __Vegetable Seeds__ action space, you can place another person on an accumulation space and get 1 additional good of the accumulating type.

I had this come up in my game as well.

https://boardgamearena.com/gamereview?table=348489977

Moves 351 and 358.

I think this depends a bit on the interpretation of whether or not the space is "providing exactly 1 animal." My feeling is that the SPACE is providing 1 animal, so you should be able to stack both ravenous hunger and pet collector.

If the interpretation is that the space now provides more than 1 animal, then technically I don't think you should have the ability to use pet collector after using ravenous hunger. Ravenous hunger text doesn't give you an option to take an extra good, you have to take the extra good. So then ravenous hunger to an animal space should always give you an extra animal, which would mean you can't use pet collector. Which is kind of a bummer in my opinion!
Pet Lover *does* work with Animal Dealer, which may be inconsistent with the Ravenous Hunger behavior. See this game for an example: https://boardgamearena.com/6/agricola?table=359195086#

detailLines: The official ruling from the publisher states that the player can receive 1 of each animal from C168 and subsequently cook those animals in order to pay the cost of 1 food per remaining harvest.

comments.text: Official ruling here: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2571263/article/36643034#36643034

That is a terrible ruling by the publisher and should be questioned. When do you ever pay after you buy something in this game? Look at Animal Dealer, Small Greenhouse, Grocer, Buyer, Haydryer, Cattle Feeder, they all would benefit from this interpretation.

And if we argue that buy and pay is different: Look at Dwelling Mound, where you have to pay before you receive the field tile, which makes it impossible to combo with Cultivator.

Another example Hardware Store, you have to pay 2 food before you receive the resources.

I could go on...

the publisher has made many questionable rulings. you can try arguing on BGG if you want, but good luck getting anywhere.

for what it's worth I disagree with your premise that Animal Dealer, etc. would benefit from this interpretation as they all describe the cost of food in the same sentence as getting the good. Animal Catcher's structure of having the cost in the sentence after the sentence describing getting the good, apparently makes a difference according to the publisher.

detailLines: Use Freshman to play an occupation via the sow/bake bread action in round 7.

At the end of round 6, a player used baking course to play an occupation for free via the freshman occupation.  In round 7, when the same player took the action sow/bake bread, he was not given the option to play an occupation via the freshman (the option did not appear - only bake bread did).  He had used Freshman multiple times previously without issue.  However, on his game log, the baking course was shown to have triggered after round 7 started, and yet on another player’s log, it was shown to have triggered before round 7 started (we’re not sure why this is the case).  The hypothesis is that the freshman wasn’t allowed to trigger via the sow/bake bread action on round 7 because the game incorrectly logged the freshman being used via baking course at the start of round 7 instead of the end of round 6 (freshman can trigger only once per round).
The player tried closing his browser, refreshing the page, etc… but the option to use freshman never came up for the sow/bake bread action.
